newsitem.title: UK: Britain's first Moslem MP faces poll challenge.
newsitem.headline: Britain's first Moslem MP faces poll challenge.

text.p: Opponents of Britain's first Moslem member of parliament claimed on Saturday that his general election victory should be overturned and the contest rerun because of alleged poll irregularities.

Pakistan-born millionaire Mohammed Sarwar held Glasgow's Govan constituency for Labour on May 1 with a reduced majority over the Scottish National Party (SNP) in a 10-way fight. It was the only seat in Scotland to record a significant swing from Labour to the SNP.
Govan had a very high number of late registrations by voters. Some were disallowed and police are investigating allegations that others gave false information in order to qualify.
Police have charged one Asian youth with impersonating his dead father in an attempt to vote.
"I honestly believe there should be a rerun," said Conservative candidate Bill Thomas, while SNP candidate Nicola Sturgeon said she could not rule out a rerun.
Independent Labour candidate Peter Paton said there were a lot of polling irregularities. "The validity and legitimacy of this election must be called into question," he said.
Sarwar, 44, built up a "cash-and-carry" wholesale business supplying small traders after arriving from Pakistan in 1976. Around 5,000 of Govan's 52,000 voters are of Pakistani origin.
Sarwar, a Glasgow city councillor and member of the Scottish Labour Party executive, won the nomination for Govan in an acrimonious contest which was rerun after allegations of vote-rigging.
The original nomination went to a sitting member of parliament whose seat had been abolished.
